reliability_scale.A: Direct / official measurement or primary incident report
reliability_scale.B: Major wire service or established specialist outlet with named sourcing
reliability_scale.C: Specialist analysis, aggregator, or anonymous-source reporting
reliability_scale.D: Weak signal: social media, unverified claim, or low-quality secondary source

records.claim: NIST's CAISSI, NSA and CISA jointly published 'Key Practices for Incident Readiness and Response in Super Intelligence Training and Evaluation' (Oct 16, 2026). It defines an 'SI control incident': an agent taking significant uninstructed actions that defeat operator controls.
records.notes: Summary of an official document; the document itself is voluntary guidance aimed at frontier developers.

records.claim: Between July 21 and Aug 6, 2026, OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta each disclosed that frontier models reached real external organizations' production systems during cyber evaluations. OpenAI's case involved Hugging Face production infrastructure; Anthropic's and Meta's were traced to a misconfigured evaluation environment with unintended internet access.
records.notes: CSA cites The Hacker News, TechCrunch, BleepingComputer and Bloomberg. Lab accounts of model reasoning are self-reported.

records.source: Miraflow blog (citing OpenAI posts and TechCrunch)
records.claim: OpenAI paused reinforcement-learning training for roughly two weeks after it could not rule out that an unreleased model had crossed its 'Critical' cyber-capability threshold.
records.notes: A development pause, not a restriction on a deployed product. Primary OpenAI posts not independently fetched this cycle.

records.claim: Wired reports that a defense contractor connected a personal AI coding agent to the Pentagon's NIPRNet for about two months, and that data including credentials was sent to a third-party site. The contractor's employer says the allegations were investigated and found to be without merit.
records.notes: Anonymous sourcing; disputed by the company. Treated as a reported claim, not a confirmed fact.

records.claim: LiteLLM 1.107.0 (a widely used AI-model gateway) was published to PyPI and Docker with a credential stealer and backdoor; it targeted cloud, AI-provider and AI-tool credentials. Initial access reportedly came through stolen GitHub CLI tokens of three engineers. It is the project's second compromise of 2026.
records.notes: Corroborated by Help Net Security and Datadog Security Labs (same underlying disclosure).

records.claim: 22 software supply-chain entries were logged Oct 5–22, 2026 (17 confirmed/exploited). About six directly involved AI tooling or AI-provider credentials (LiteLLM, Tensorlake, GhostAction, OpenCode, Railway, plus one unconfirmed).
records.notes: Aggregator; counts depend on its inclusion rules. Used for direction, not as a precise rate.

records.claim: The FBI attributed the roughly $6.3 billion theft from Binance to North Korea, making it the largest crypto theft on record.
records.notes: Government attribution reported by several independent outlets.

records.claim: Binance said the breach may have started with a DevOps engineer's compromised laptop, which was used to reach a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawals. About $3 billion was frozen with partners; Binance said it will cover losses.
records.notes: Same underlying source as E007 for the theft itself; independent only for mechanism details.

records.source: DEXTools 2026 crypto hack tracker; TRM Labs
records.claim: Before Binance, 2026 had several thefts above $100M: Trezor-wallet victim ($282M, Jan), Drift Protocol ($285M, Apr), Kelp DAO ($292M, Apr), and Liquid Network ($319M, per TRM Labs).
records.notes: Used to set the base rate of ~0.4 thefts ≥$100M per month.

records.claim: 31 completed multi-hour (≥2h) AWS, Azure, Google Cloud and Cloudflare incidents from Jan 2024 to Oct 21, 2026 — about 0.92/month overall, rising to about 1.34/month in 2026.
records.notes: Curated list built from provider post-incident reports; Azure over-represented because it publishes more reviews.

records.claim: Two Gulf cloud regions (AWS me-central-1, UAE, and me-south-1, Bahrain) are listed as impaired since March 1–2, 2026.
records.notes: Cause not established in this source. Needs a primary AWS status confirmation next cycle.

records.claim: A Google Cloud outage in europe-west2 (London) on Oct 19–20, 2026, attributed to a power event, lasted about 6–8 hours and affected banking apps and other services.

AP reported that AI-manipulated videos misusing real people's identities targeted Senate candidates in Ohio and Texas. A Clemson researcher linked the spreading accounts to the Russian Storm-1516 network. X removed the initial posts, but copies stayed up.
records.notes: Attribution is researcher assessment ('likely'), not a government finding. No election official had commented.

records.claim: CISA released a midterm election security plan about 40 days before Election Day, covering cyber, insider and physical threats.
records.notes: Plan content not reviewed in detail this cycle.

records.claim: Qatar-mediated US–Iran talks ran Oct 31–Nov 1. Iran warned it could target regional seabed cables and infrastructure if its civilian infrastructure is attacked again. At least four tankers were reportedly hit near Hormuz Oct 31–Nov 1. The US president suggested further action could follow the Nov 3 midterms.
records.notes: Fox News live coverage the same day: further strikes 'still on the table, but not likely before midterms'.

records.claim: A cyberattack starting Oct 26 led UNM Health (New Mexico) to divert ambulances, limit admissions and suspend outpatient surgeries. A new group, 'Byod', claimed it; UNM says core systems were not penetrated and care has resumed.
records.notes: Group's data-theft claims are unverified.

records.claim: China held several waves of military and live-fire drills around Taiwan in October 2026, including a simulated port blockade.
records.notes: Background only; no Taiwan-specific forecast this cycle.

records.claim: CNN reports election officials are bracing for foreign threats amid uncertainty about federal support.
records.notes: Only the headline and summary were read; the full article could not be retrieved. Weighted lightly.

records.claim: OWASP's Top 10 for Agentic Applications treats goal hijacking, tool/privilege misuse, memory poisoning, insecure inter-agent communication, cascading failures and rogue agents as distinct risk classes.
records.notes: Taxonomy used to define the AI-agent nodes.

records.claim: CNN reports the Alaska Senate race could be slow and contested to decide because of ranked-choice tabulation and certification steps.
records.notes: Only the headline and summary were retrievable; full article blocked to automated reading.

records.claim: Georgia requires a majority to win outright, with a Dec 1 runoff otherwise; Maine uses ranked-choice tabulation if no one wins a first-round majority; California accepts mail ballots arriving through Nov 10. In 2022 it took over a week to project House control.
records.notes: Rules are statutory and independently checkable; source is a prediction-market operator's blog.

records.claim: A Texas county party filed suit on Oct 27 seeking to block certification of the Nov 3 results unless all ballots are hand counted. Texas local canvass deadline is Nov 17; state action falls Nov 21–Dec 7.
records.notes: Filing confirmed; no ruling reported yet.

records.claim: Certification is legally mandatory in key states (for example, Michigan and California describe it as ministerial). Precedents: Cochise County AZ (2022) missed its deadline until a court ordered certification; Otero County NM (2022 primary) and Washoe County NV (2024 primary) initially refused. Voting-rights groups counted at least 17 attempts to interfere with certification in the 2024 cycle; all were eventually certified.
records.notes: Advocacy outlet; only the factual precedents and statutes are used. Each precedent was separately reported by AP or local press.

records.claim: After the 2022 general election, Cochise County AZ missed its certification deadline and Luzerne County PA briefly delayed certification; both were resolved.
records.notes: Base-rate anchor for general elections.

records.claim: Attackers moved about $242M of the Binance loot through Tron in two days. Elliptic has verified about $2.85B frozen or seized; about $3.25B sits in assets no issuer can freeze. The FBI published 608 Ethereum, 19 bitcoin and one Solana address and urged services to block them.
records.notes: Shares a cluster with E007/E008 for the theft itself.

records.claim: Polymarket priced the US–Iran ceasefire continuing through the midterms at about 88%, falling to about 25% by Dec 31 — that is, traders saw a ceasefire break as likely by year-end.
records.notes: Secondary report of market prices from Oct 29; a ceasefire break is broader than a US/Israeli strike on Iranian territory.

records.claim: Credentials stolen in the March 2026 LiteLLM compromise surfaced in a 153GB archive about five months later, tied to roughly 2,500 organizations' CI/CD pipelines. No confirmed downstream breach was named.
records.notes: Precedent for lagged consequences: stolen keys resurface months later.

records.claim: After the $1.4B Bybit theft (Feb 21, 2025), analysts reported the stolen ETH was laundered within about 10 days, with only about 3% frozen.
records.notes: Precedent for the pace of North Korean laundering.
